cases.C14: Vouchsafe's archaic grace suits governed trust; despite Vouchsafe.id, sector differs sharply—identity verification versus agent permissioning—reducing real buyer confusion.
cases.C26: Far from frail, 'chary' precisely signals principled, institutional vigilance. Paired with 'Labs' in enterprise context, CFOs and CISOs will never confuse it with charity, ensuring total uncrowded distinctiveness.
cases.C12: Despite narrow tool uses like veto.so, 'Veto Labs' commands instant enterprise authority, brilliantly packaging human-in-the-loop governance for UK CISOs with unmistakable, boardroom-ready clarity across .co.uk and .ai.
cases.C27: Anchorite Labs turns obscurity into gravitas: a chosen, walled-in cell exactly mirrors least-privilege agents awaiting human approval. Clear UK registration and domains; inactive US namesake poses no active conflict.
cases.C23: Pentera differs in syllables and context; Penstock Group is healthcare payments, not AI agents. A sluice-gate exactly names metered, revocable capability — sober, memorable, ownable.
cases.C17: No major AI/security clash; rarity buys distinctiveness. Pronunciation: SEN-uh-shul. If premium domains are gone, the name still earns recall and trademark clarity.
cases.C24: Pronunciation is straightforward (CLAW-strah Labs), as in French architecture. The cloister root signals trusted enclosure, not phobia. Sober, ownable, and the perforated-screen metaphor perfectly captures 'information flows only where it may' for security-conscious buyers.
cases.C11: Distinct spelling from Cautio and a different sector (AI trust vs dashcams) means confusion is unlikely. The Latin cautio legal-bond root suits regulated buyers, and the concise form is memorable once heard.
cases.C29: Archaic = timeless infrastructure vocabulary. 'Seneschal' perfectly encodes delegated-authority thesis; 'Labs' signals engineering rigor. Phonetic once heard, zero AI competitors, CISOs respect precise terminology.
cases.C30: Provost evokes delegated authority and oversight, aligning with the trust‑by‑consent model; its academic gravitas reinforces credibility for CISOs, while “Labs” signals innovative engineering, not a university office.
cases.C22: The offshore association is subtle; for CISOs, 'bailiwick' primarily signals precise jurisdictional control and strict authority, perfectly mirroring the architecture of distrust.
cases.C31: The Roman metaphor transforms a common term into an image of imperial-grade stability. 'Labs' differentiates the consultancy-led model from the pure-play software of existing Vallum entities.
cases.C16: Imprimatur Labs perfectly encodes the core thesis: human approval gates risky actions. Ecclesiastical roots fade beside the vivid modern meaning of official sanction. Memorable, ownable, and sober enough for any CISO.
cases.C18: Redoubt's defensive metaphor is precise: contained agents, bounded capabilities, approval walls. Domain scarcity is real; survivalist association is marginal and easily displaced by consistent security-first positioning. Strong enough to overcome.
